active.reliability: The 2.5L and conventional automatic have a generally durable record, but 165k miles makes rust, suspension wear, mounts and maintenance history decisive. The listing reports an accident, so inspection is essential.
active.safety: IIHS named the 2012 Mazda3 a Top Safety Pick with Good original front, side, roof and head-restraint results. The listing shows stability control; confirm operation and open-recall status by VIN.
active.verdict: Best balance of reliability and crash protection
active.note: This remains the most convincing first-car candidate in the verified group. Inspect the body and undercarriage closely and review the accident history before treating its model reputation as proof of this car’s condition.

active.reliability: The 1.8L engine and conventional automatic have a strong durability record, but 189k miles makes oil use, water-pump leaks, suspension wear, transmission service and Northeast rust important checks. Require service records and an independent inspection.
active.safety: IIHS named the 2010 Corolla a Top Safety Pick, with Good original moderate-front, side, roof-strength and head-restraint ratings. The listing shows stability control; confirm operation and check this VIN for open recalls.
active.verdict: Strong reliability and crash protection, with dealer-fee caution
active.note: This is one of today’s best first-car prospects because reliability and safety are both strong. The advertised price is $3,999, but recent dealer reviews mention substantial added fees, so get a written out-the-door figure before traveling.

active.reliability: The 1.8L engine and conventional 5-speed automatic are generally durable and inexpensive to service, but 203k miles creates substantial wear exposure. Inspect engine mounts, suspension, wheel bearings, cooling system, leaks and maintenance history.
active.safety: IIHS named the 2013 Civic sedan a Top Safety Pick+ with Good ratings in driver small-overlap, original moderate-front, side, roof and head-restraint tests. Stability control and curtain airbags were standard; check the VIN for open recalls.
active.verdict: Excellent crash record and durable drivetrain, tempered by 203k miles
active.note: The Civic’s safety and mechanical reputation make it a serious first-car candidate despite the odometer. Only unusually good records and a clean independent inspection should justify buying a car over 200k miles.

active.reliability: The 5-speed manual avoids the troublesome PowerShift dual-clutch automatic that hurts this generation’s reputation. At 160k miles, inspect the clutch, cooling system, engine mounts, suspension and Northeast rust.
active.safety: IIHS named the 2012 Focus a Top Safety Pick, with Good original moderate-front, side, roof and head-restraint ratings plus an Acceptable small-overlap result. Stability control and curtain airbags were standard; verify operation and VIN recalls.
active.verdict: Strong crash protection without the infamous automatic
active.note: This is a sensible first-car prospect if your son can drive a manual. The listing says one owner, but only service records and an independent inspection can establish this car’s condition.

active.reliability: The manual transmission avoids high-mileage CVT exposure, but the 2.0L can consume oil and 177k miles brings clutch, wheel-bearing, suspension and rust risk. Check oil level history and cold-start behavior closely.
active.safety: IIHS ratings for the 2016 wagon include Good small-overlap, moderate-front, side, roof and head-restraint results. Stability control and curtain airbags were standard; this manual trim does not have EyeSight.
active.verdict: Excellent crash shell, with high-mileage wear to audit
active.note: The manual gearbox and strong crashworthiness make this a compelling winter-capable first car. It ranks below the Focus because mileage and Subaru oil-consumption and wheel-bearing exposure raise repair risk.

active.reliability: The 2.0L/automatic combination is relatively simple and generally durable. Demand proof of timing-belt service and inspect for Northeast rust, suspension wear and oil leaks.
active.safety: IIHS rated moderate-overlap front and head restraints Good; cars built after November 2009 also earned a Good side rating. This car’s build date and electronic stability control were not verified, so confirm both.
active.verdict: Promising low-mileage value, with safety details to confirm
active.note: At 125k miles, this has the lowest mileage among the stronger-reliability choices. It stays near the top only if the build-date label, stability-control equipment and timing-belt records check out.

active.reliability: This older Focus uses a conventional automatic, not the later PowerShift unit, and its 2.0L drivetrain is generally durable. Low mileage is attractive, but age means rust, mounts, suspension, seals and long storage intervals still need scrutiny.
active.safety: IIHS ratings applying to 2008–11 models are Good for original moderate-front and head restraints and Acceptable for side impact. Curtain and torso airbags were standard, but electronic stability control was not verified for this car.
active.verdict: Simple low-mileage drivetrain, older safety design
active.note: At 93k miles this is mechanically appealing, but its crash protection and unverified stability control trail the newer Focus and Impreza. Confirm the odometer history and inspect for corrosion from age and Northeast use.

active.reliability: The 3.3L Lambda V6 avoids the later Sonata’s notorious 2.4L Theta II pattern and is usually durable, but adds fuel and repair cost. Check oil leaks, charging system, suspension, cooling system and rust.
active.safety: IIHS ratings applying to the 2009 Sonata are Good for original moderate-overlap front, side and head restraints. The listing shows stability control; verify the equipment and recall status on the car.
active.verdict: Good crash protection and reasonable mechanical odds
active.note: This is a sensible midsize first-car candidate if the V6’s higher fuel and insurance costs fit. A clean cold start, rust-free underside and maintenance file matter more than the attractive price.

active.reliability: The conventional 4-speed automatic avoids later Subaru CVT risk, but at 168k miles the 2.5L needs proof of timing-belt service and careful checks for head-gasket or oil leaks, wheel bearings, suspension and rust.
active.safety: IIHS named the non-WRX 2011 Impreza a Top Safety Pick with Good original moderate-front, side, roof and head-restraint ratings. Stability control and curtain airbags were standard; verify Takata recall completion by VIN.
active.verdict: Strong crash protection with a conventional automatic
active.note: This lead combines good crashworthiness with a transmission that avoids CVT exposure. It still needs timing-belt records, a cold-start inspection and a rust-focused underbody check.

active.reliability: The 3.0L Duratec V6 and conventional 4-speed automatic have a generally serviceable record, but 147k miles and Northeast age raise transmission, cooling-system, suspension, wheel-bearing and structural-rust risk. Inspect the rear wheel wells, subframes and 4WD system closely.
active.safety: IIHS rated the 2008 Escape Acceptable in the original moderate-front test, Good in side impact, Marginal for roof strength and Acceptable for head restraints. This listing verifies standard side-curtain airbags, ABS and AdvanceTrac stability control; open-recall status still needs a VIN check.
active.verdict: Useful safety equipment and a low price, with older-SUV compromises
active.note: Standard stability control and curtain airbags are important positives for a new driver, while the only-Acceptable frontal result and Marginal roof rating prevent a stronger safety grade. At $2,499 it is worth inspecting, but rust and automatic-transmission condition are deal-breakers.

active.reliability: At 207k miles, this Outback carries substantial CVT valve-body and wear risk plus possible oil consumption, wheel-bearing, suspension and Northeast-rust costs. A Subaru-specialist inspection and strong fluid-service records are essential.
active.safety: IIHS ratings applying to 2015–19 Outbacks are Good in small-overlap, moderate-front, side, roof and head-restraint tests. Stability control and curtain airbags were standard; the listing does not verify optional EyeSight.
active.verdict: Excellent crash protection, very high repair exposure
active.note: This is a strong crash-protection option, but its mileage and CVT keep it well below the simpler cars. Consider it only with unusually complete records, a clean cold-to-hot road test and an independent inspection.

active.reliability: The 3.3L V6 and conventional automatic avoid Hyundai’s later 2.4L Theta pattern, but 197k miles brings substantial AWD, cooling, suspension, wheel-bearing, leak and rust exposure. Inspect the subframes and underbody closely.
active.safety: IIHS named the 2008 Santa Fe a Top Safety Pick with Good original moderate-front, side and head-restraint results. Stability control and curtain airbags were standard; its age means no modern small-overlap rating or driver-assistance systems.
active.verdict: Good older crash record, very high mileage
active.note: Its size, standard stability control and strong original crash tests suit a teen better than many cheap SUVs. The mileage and Northeast rust risk make a full independent inspection non-negotiable.
